headline: Australia declares West Peron storage formation for INPEX-led Bonaparte CCS
summary: Australia's federal government formally declared the West Peron formation (permit G-7-AP, ~260 km off Darwin) an identified greenhouse gas storage formation — the country's first such declaration for an offshore saline aquifer, clearing a key regulatory gate for the Bonaparte CCS project ahead of a future FID.
co2crc_note: Landmark first Australian offshore saline-aquifer storage declaration — directly central to CO2CRC's domestic CCS mission and the national storage-resource pipeline.
extractor_note: Government declaration (not FID or injection approval). Sources cite up to ~443 Mt total over ~35 yr and roughly 8-10 Mtpa; capacity_mtpa set to 10 (upper cited rate, not approved injection).

headline: Worley Rosenberg wins Subsea7 fabrication contract for Northern Lights Phase II
summary: Worley's Rosenberg yard will fabricate subsea spools and structures for the Phase II expansion of Norway's Northern Lights (Longship) project, which lifts CO2 transport-and-storage capacity from 1.5 Mtpa to more than 5 Mtpa by 2028; Subsea7 is Equinor's technical service provider for the phase.
co2crc_note: Supply-chain execution on Europe's flagship open-access CO2 T&S network — a reference model for Australian cross-user storage hubs.
extractor_note: Contract award; value undisclosed. capacity_mtpa 5 is the Phase II expansion target, not this contract's scope.

headline: One Earth Energy scales back Illinois CO2 storage project to a single injection well
summary: The ethanol producer's subsidiary cut its eastern McLean County plan from three injection wells to one (plus four monitoring wells and a 5.4-mile, 8-inch pipeline near Saybrook) as it revives post-moratorium; it still needs an EPA Class VI permit and an Illinois Commerce Commission certificate amid Mahomet Aquifer objections.
co2crc_note: Illustrates US permitting and social-licence friction (aquifer protection) reshaping project scope — context for storage characterisation and community engagement.
extractor_note: Scope reduction (3 wells to 1), not a cancellation; project proceeding at reduced scale pending permits.

headline: Frontier buyers sign ~US$11.7M in-situ mineralisation removal deal with Oman's 44.01
summary: Frontier's advance-market buyers (Stripe, Google, Shopify, Autodesk, H&M Group, Workday and others via Watershed) committed ~US$11.7M for ~20,932 tonnes of CO2 removal delivered 2028-2031 using 44.01's peridotite mineralisation — Frontier's first in-situ mineralisation purchase.
co2crc_note: Validates permanent mineralisation storage pathway and corporate CDR demand — a storage modality adjacent to CO2CRC's saline-aquifer focus.
extractor_note: Removal offtake/purchase (~20,932 t total over 2028-2031), not an annual capacity; capacity_mtpa left null.

headline: Wood Mackenzie: global CO2 transport sector to reach ~US$211bn by 2060, APAC ~60% of spend
summary: A new Wood Mackenzie report projects ~US$211bn of global CO2 transport investment by 2060, enabling ~3 Gtpa moved with ~200 Mtpa crossing borders; Asia Pacific accounts for ~60% of spend, pipelines dominate, and the storage mismatch is driving cross-border CO2 trade and liquefied-CO2 shipping.
co2crc_note: APAC-centric transport outlook underscores the cross-border CO2 shipping/trade opportunity central to Australia's export-storage ambitions (Bonaparte, Bayu-Undan).
extractor_note: Market-aggregate forecast (US$211bn by 2060), not a discrete commitment; amount left null per golden rules.

headline: Plans to add hydrogen and carbon capture to a Yorkshire waste incinerator challenged
summary: Proposals to retrofit hydrogen and carbon capture to a waste-to-energy incinerator in Yorkshire face a local challenge — the latest UK community-consent flashpoint for energy-from-waste CCS retrofits.
co2crc_note: Another UK social-licence flashpoint for EfW carbon capture — watch for consent-process lessons transferable to Australian projects.
extractor_note: Community/planning challenge to an EfW-CCS retrofit; social-licence item.
